messages.subject: Re: Rstan as zipped library
parts:
Hi David,

I think you should be able to get rstan working. If the computer in question has the prerequistes --- Rtools and the Rcpp package (which is best installed from source) plus the R packages BH, RcppEigen, inline, KernSmooth (which can be installed from binaries) --- then you should be able to download https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.5.0/rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz on an unsecured computer and copy it to the in computer in question. Then execute in R

install.packages(file.path("path", "to", "rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz"), type = "source")

which will try to install rstan from (for example) C:\path\to\rstan_2.5.0.tar.gz .

Ben

On Wed, Nov 19, 2014 at 7:27 AM, David Kitska (Contractor) wrote:
Hello Ben,
 
Please forgive me for contacting you via email rather than posting this question in the Stan users group.  I seem unable to post from my unclassified PC at work!
 
In short, I work at a government secured lab which forbids direct connections between our PCs and the internet.  Hence, I am unable to load Rstan on my work PC by running the install script from within R.  Will the entire Rstan package become available in zipped format so that it could first be downloaded, saved to disk, then installed from the zipped file, as I currently do for regular R packages? 
 
Thank you for your time!
 
Dave Kitska
